headword: {自転車操業|じてんしゃそうぎょう}
reading: じてんしゃそうぎょう
gloss: hand-to-mouth operation; running on borrowed money

definitions.gloss: hand-to-mouth business; keeping afloat by constant borrowing
definitions.explanation: A business, or a household, that survives only by constantly bringing in new money, often new loans, to pay off earlier debts. Like a bicycle that falls over when it stops, it collapses as soon as the cash flow stops.

examples.japanese: うちの⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{自転車操業|じてんしゃそうぎょう}だ。
examples.english: Our company is running hand to mouth.

examples.japanese: ⟦{借金|しゃっきん}→借金：03203_shakkin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{借金|しゃっきん}→借金：03203_shakkin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{返|かえ}す→返す：09648_kaesu⟧{自転車操業|じてんしゃそうぎょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いている→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: We keep paying off debts with new debts, just barely staying afloat.

examples.japanese: ⟦{売上|うりあげ}→売上：04102_uriage⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すこ}しでも→少しでも：19718_sukoshidemo⟧⟦{落|お}ちれば→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧、{自転車操業|じてんしゃそうぎょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{小|ちい}さな→小さな：02913_chiisana⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧はすぐに{行|ゆ}き{詰|づ}まってしまう。
examples.english: If sales drop even a little, a small shop running hand to mouth soon reaches a dead end.

notes:
A metaphor from riding a bicycle: you must keep pedaling or you fall. Used about companies and also, jokingly, about personal finances or any schedule that leaves no slack.
